(Surat al-Taghabun is Medinan, and it has eighteen verses.)

(In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.)

To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things capable.﴾ ﴿He is the One who created you; among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. So they tasted the bad consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and God was self-sufficient. And God is Rich and Praiseworthy.﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did, and that is easy for God."﴾ ﴿So believe in God and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down. And God is Aware of what you do.﴾ ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾ .

This surah is Medinan according to most scholars. Ibn ʿAbbas and others said it is Meccan except for some of its final verses, from "O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children..." (64:14) onward, which were revealed in Medina. Al-Kalbi said it is both Medinan and Meccan. The connection of this surah to what precedes it is that the preceding surah deals with the state of the hypocrites, and at its end it addresses the believers. So it follows that with what suits it, namely His saying: ﴿He is the One who created you; among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer.﴾ This is a division in faith and disbelief with regard to acquisition, according to a group of commentators, in light of his saying (ﷺ): "Every child is born upon the fitrah (natural disposition)," and the saying of the Exalted: ﴿the fitrah of God upon which He created mankind﴾ (30:30). It was also said that these two states are in the origin of creation, as evidenced by what is in the hadith of the drop of semen, concerning the angel's saying: "Is he wretched or fortunate?" And the boy whom al-Khidr (peace be upon him) killed was sealed as a disbeliever on the day he was sealed. And what Ibn Masʿud narrated: that he (ﷺ) said, "God created Pharaoh in the womb as a disbeliever." Yahya ibn Zakariyya related that he was a believer in the womb. And from ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah concerning ﴿among you is a disbeliever﴾ (p-277) in God: he is a believer in the star, and a believer in God who disbelieves in the star. He put the disbeliever first because of his large number. Do you not see His saying, ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ (34:13)? And when He mentioned the righteous, He said, ﴿and few are they﴾ (38:24).

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Among you is one who comes with disbelief and performs it, and among you is one who comes with faith and performs it, like His saying: ﴿And We placed in their descendants prophethood and the Book, so among them is one who is guided, and many of them are defiant﴾ (57:26). The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿and God is Seeing of what you do,﴾ meaning: He is Knower of your disbelief and your faith, which are from your side. The meaning is: He is the One who bestowed upon you the foundation of blessings, which is creation and bringing into existence from non-existence, so you should have looked with correct insight and all of you should have been grateful servants." End of quotation. This is in the manner of the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school). He also said: It was said: "He is the One who created you; among you is a disbeliever" in the creation, these are the Dahriyya (those who deny a Creator and attribute existence to time), "and among you is a believer" in it. From al-Hasan: there is an ellipsis in the speech, indicated by its estimated form: "and among you is a defiant one." It seems this is from the lies of the Mu'tazilah against al-Hasan.

The prepositional phrase came first in His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: "By placing both of them first, it indicates the meaning of the exclusivity of dominion and praise to God, the Mighty and Majestic. This is because dominion in truth belongs to Him, since He is the originator of everything and its creator, and the one who sustains it and oversees it. Likewise praise, since the foundations and branches of blessings are from Him. As for the dominion of others, it is a delegation from Him. And their praise is a recognition that God's blessing came through their hands."

The majority read (ṣuwarakum) with a ḍammah on the ṣād. Zayd ibn ʿAli and Abu Razin read it with a kasrah, though the analogical form is with ḍammah. This is an enumeration of the blessing of beautiful creation, since the limbs of the children of Adam function in all the ways that the limbs of animals function, and with many additional features by which they are distinguished. Then he is distinguished by the beauty of the face and the excellence of the bodily members, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾ (95:4). It was also said: the blessing here is only the human form insofar as he is a human who perceives and reasons. This is what was made beautiful for him, so that he attained many perfections. The Arabs scarcely knew "ṣūrah" except as shape, not as the meaning that subsists within the form.

The Exalted drew attention to His knowledge of what is in the heavens and the earth, then to His knowledge of what the servants keep secret and what they make public, then to His knowledge of what the breasts contain, to show that nothing escapes His knowledge, neither the universals nor the particulars. So He began with the knowledge that encompasses the entire world, then with the specific servants in their secret and public affairs, then with what is particular to them, which is what their breasts contain of hidden and concealed things. All of this carries the meaning of a warning, since He, the Exalted, is the one who recompenses all of that with reward and punishment.

The majority read ﴿what you keep secret and what you make public﴾ with the second-person ta' (addressing you). ʿUbayd from Abu ʿAmr and Aban from ʿAsim read it with the third-person ya' (they).

In it there is a hint of Mu'tazilite doctrine. The claim (al-zaʿm) was explained earlier. ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾ refers to the people of Mecca. ﴿Yes (bala)﴾ is an affirmation of what follows a negative particle. ﴿And that is easy for God﴾ means: nothing diverts Him from it.

﴿For the Day of Gathering﴾: on that day the first and the last are gathered, because each one is resurrected hoping for deliverance and elevation of rank.

﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾: this is a metaphor drawn from people who engage in trade and cheat one another (taghābana al-qawm fī al-tijārah), which is when they defraud one another. This is because the blessed will be placed in the stations of the wretched had they been wretched, and the wretched will be placed in the stations of the blessed had they been blessed. From Mujahid and others: when the recompense takes place, the believers will have defrauded the disbelievers, because they enter Paradise while the disbelievers are confined to the Fire. Al-Aʿraj, Shaybah, Abu Jaʿfar, Talhah, Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿAsim, Zayd ibn ʿAli, and al-Hasan, with one variant from him, read ﴿We will remove﴾ and ﴿We will admit him﴾ with nun in both. Al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa, al-Hasan, and the rest of the seven readers read them with ya' in both.

And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful.﴾ ﴿If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing.﴾ ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

It is singled out for mention, although all events occur only by the permission of Allah. It has been said: it is possible that by "calamity" is meant any occurrence, whether good or evil, since the wisdom in its occurring is by the permission of Allah. The feminine marker (ta') did not attach to asaba even though the subject is feminine, which is eloquent usage. We seek refuge in Allah from trials. Wealth was mentioned before children because it is the greater trial: ﴿Nay! Indeed, man transgresses when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Alaq: 6]; ﴿Our wealth and our families have occupied us﴾ [al-Fath: 11].

"And listen" to what you are admonished with, "and obey" in what you are commanded and forbidden, "and spend" in what is obligatory upon you. "Khayran" is in the accusative by a deleted verb whose estimate is: "and bring about good," or by the implied "yakun" so that it becomes the predicate, or as an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, meaning: "a good spending," or as a circumstantial accusative, or as an object of "and spend good," meaning wealth. Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 64, verses 11–18:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification.﴾ ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive – then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.﴾ ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful.﴾ ﴿If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing.﴾ ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

The apparent meaning is that "calamity" (musibah) applies to any misfortune or what distresses the servant, that is, in his self, his wealth, his child, his speech, or his action. It is singled out for mention, although all events occur only by the permission of Allah. It has been said: it is possible that by "calamity" is meant any occurrence, whether good or evil, since the wisdom in its occurring is by the permission of Allah. Ma here is negative, and the object of asaba is omitted, meaning: it does not befall anyone. The subject is "min musibah," and "min" is extra. The feminine marker (ta') did not attach to asaba even though the subject is feminine, which is eloquent usage. The feminine form is found in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No nation precedes its term﴾ [al-Hijr: 5], and His saying: "And no sign comes to them except by the permission of Allah," meaning: by His will, His knowledge, and His enabling.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾ means: he affirms His existence and knows that every occurrence is by His decree and destiny. ﴿He will guide his heart﴾ to the path of good and guidance. Al-Jumhur read yahdi with the ya', as the present tense of hada, jussed as an answer to the conditional. Ibn Jubayr, Talhah, Ibn Hurmuz, and al-Azraq from Hamzah read it with the nun (nahdi). Al-Sulami, al-Dahhak, and Abu Ja'far read yuhda in the passive, with qalbuhu as the subject in the nominative. Ikrimah, Amr ibn Dinar, and Malik ibn Dinar read (yahda'), with a sukun hamzah, and qalbuhu in the nominative: his heart becomes tranquil and settled through his faith, and there is no agitation in it. Amr ibn Fa'id read yahda with an alif replacing the sukun hamzah. Ikrimah and Malik ibn Dinar also read yahda, with the alif after its substitution for the sukun hamzah deleted; the substitution of hamzah with alif in words like yahda' and yaqra' is not analogical, contrary to those who permitted it as analogy and built upon it the permissibility of deleting that alif for the jussive. On this basis was explained the verse of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma:

"Whoever wrongs will be punished for his wrong swiftly, and whoever does not begin with wrong will not be wronged."

Its original form is yabda', then he replaced the hamzah with an alif, then deleted it for the jussive, likening it to the alif of yakhsha when the jussive particle enters.

When Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah,﴾ and then commanded obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, and warned against what befalls a man from his wife and child because of the enmity that issues from some of them, and there is no greater enemy to a man than his wife and child if they are enemies, and that is in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, it is by the ruin of his wealth and honor; as for the Hereafter, it is by what he strives to acquire of the unlawful for them, and by what they gain from it because of his position. How many a woman has killed her husband, cut him off, and corrupted his mind, and how many a child has killed his father. There is much of this in the histories and in what we have witnessed of it. From Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: that Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i wanted to go on raid with the Prophet ﷺ, but his family and children gathered and discouraged him and complained to him of his separation, so he relented and did not go. Then he regretted punishing them, and it was revealed: ﴿That is because those who disbelieved﴾ [Muhammad: 3], the verse. It has been said: a people believed in Allah, but their wives and children discouraged them from emigration, and they did not emigrate until after a period; then they found that others had gained understanding in the religion, so they regretted, were grieved, and resolved to punish their wives and children, and it was revealed. It has been said: they said to them, "Where will you go, leaving your land, your kin, and your wealth?" So they became angry with them and said, "If Allah gathers us in the abode of emigration, we will not benefit you with good." When they emigrated, they withheld good from them, so they wished that they would pardon them and return to them kindness and connection. The "min" in ﴿among your wives and your children﴾ is partitive, for a wife may be found who gladdens her husband and helps him toward his aims in his religion and his worldly life, and likewise a child. The Abasi poet said, praising his son as a protective shield:

"When the children of men are a bitterness, you are the sweet, cool, sweet-tasting sweetness (halal)."

"For us is a side of him that is soft, and a side that is difficult to ride when enemies attempt it."

"And in noble deeds he is seized with a quiver, as the moist branch quivers beneath the wind."

Qarman ibn al-A'raf said about his son Munazil, who was disobedient to him, a poem of some length, from which:

"I raised him until, when I left him a man of the people, and his beard had grown beyond the need for wiping..."

"When he saw me, he thought the near figure was a far figure, and I was approaching the far figure."

"He deliberately wronged me and twisted my hand; may Allah, who is its overpowerer, twist his hand."
